background: Operator's post-#1318 governing order, item 1: TP-DMX-PR1304-RED-LANE-PATH-REGEX-HARDENING-001. Python's `$` matches immediately before a trailing newline (not strictly end-of-string), and `.` never crosses a newline without re.DOTALL. A control character embedded in a file_path could make an `^`-anchored, `.*$`-tailed DCP-RED-MERGE-SEAM-0001 FORBIDDEN_PATHS entry fail to match anywhere in the string (silent fall-through to unblocked) or make a negative-lookahead exemption falsely treat a control-character-suffixed string as the real exempted file. Previously recorded as an INFORMATIONAL 'no realistic bypass' finding (proof/TP-DMX-DCP-WORKFLOW-SEAM-LIFT-001R/FINAL_AUDIT_VERDICT.json, F3). ADR-226 Amendment A5a is about to add three more exemptions to this same matcher, so this closes the anchoring imprecision at the source: every FORBIDDEN_PATHS pattern now anchors with \Z instead of $, every .*-containing pattern compiles with re.DOTALL, and surface_guard_block gains an unconditional, independent control-character fail-closed check as defense in depth. Round 2: a Copilot review finding (round-1 tests only exercised the control-character short-circuit, never the regex anchoring fix itself) was addressed by adding a direct FORBIDDEN_PATHS.search() assertion, then squashing into one clean content commit and re-auditing.
